summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency and compliance needs for financial services. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; primary concerns: GDPR, data residency, audit logs retention, KMS/BYOK, and restricted logging for payment card data. Agreed to share security docs and follow-up technical deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We're on for 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:06] Rachel Lee: Rachel Lee, Head of Security at Horizon. Sorry, bit of background noise on my side.
[00:10] Tom Bennett: Tom Bennett, CTO.
[00:13] Aaron Miles: Aaron, Compliance.
[00:15] Olivia Park: Great, Mateo from our tech team is with me — Mateo can jump in for the deep bits.
[00:20] Mateo Ruiz: Hi all.
[00:22] Sana Iqbal: Sana, platform eng. We run most of infra in us-east and a smaller region in eu-west.
[00:28] Olivia Park: Thanks. Quick context from our side — Redwood provides hosted inference + dedicated pools and private deployments. Today we'd like to understand your residency and compliance constraints to recommend the right deployment.
[00:40] Tom Bennett: High level: we are a regional bank with retail and small business customers. We need to ensure customer PII doesn't leave EU for EU customers, and US customers' data stays in US for certain products. We're evaluating Hosted first but likely need Dedicated or Private for some flows.
[00:57] Rachel Lee: Key regs: GDPR for EU customers, PCI scoping for cardholder data, and internal policies that restrict sending full PANs or certain tokens to third-party hosted services. Also need strong audit logs, tamper-evident, and retention controls.
[01:14] Olivia Park: Understood. Can you describe the flows you expect to send to an LLM? Are you sending raw payment data? PII?
[01:21] Tom Bennett: We're exploring chat assistants for customers and agents, and embeddings for search. We would never intentionally send full PANs, but there are edge cases in chat transcripts where customers might paste numbers. We also have case notes with account numbers and SSNs sometimes.
[01:36] Aaron Miles: So the question is — can Redwood guarantee data locality and prevent logs from being stored outside jurisdiction, and can we control what's logged?
[01:44] Mateo Ruiz: Short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be region-restricted but is multi-tenant and has broader controls; if strict residency and isolation are required, we recommend Dedicated or Private. We support VPC peering for Private deployments and on-prem options — and BYOK/KMS integrations.
[02:00] Rachel Lee: For GDPR we need data subject access, right to be forgotten paths, and data mapping. How do you handle deletion and audit trails?
[02:08] Mateo Ruiz: For Dedicated and Private, customers can opt out of long-term logging and we can disable persistent transcript retention. For Hosted, we have retention windows and redact options but it's harder to offer customer-managed keys. We provide deletion APIs and can surface events in audit logs — though Hosted customer-managed KMS is limited today.
[02:30] Rachel Lee: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and any certifications for EU processing? Also, who's the subprocesser for hosted?
[02:36] Olivia Park: We are SOC 2 Type II; we'll send the report. For hosted, subprocessors include cloud provider infra (we'll share the list). For Dedicated/Private, you control the infra and subprocessors.
[02:49] Tom Bennett: What about encryption at rest and in transit and the ability to BYOK?
[02:54] Mateo Ruiz: TLS in transit for all traffic. Encryption at rest by default; BYOK available for Dedicated and Private via KMS integrations (AWS KMS customer key or vault integrations for on-prem). Hosted supports provider-managed keys only currently.
[03:10] Sana Iqbal: Logging — we have strict PCI scopes. Anything that touches PAN must be in-scope and logged but also we cannot allow logs that contain PAN to leave certain environments. Can Redwood mask or filter logs before they are persisted?
[03:25] Mateo Ruiz: We have request/response filters and can advise on prompt engineering to strip sensitive fields client-side. On Dedicated/Private you can disable server-side transcript retention or ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding. We also support disabling token-level logging on private deployments to avoid storing raw inputs.
[03:46] Aaron Miles: For auditing, we need tamper-evident logs and a clear chain of custody. Can we integrate with our existing audit tools?
[03:52] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we can forward logs to your logging endpoints (Syslog/CloudWatch/Elastic) and provide signed audit events. On Private you have full control. For Hosted we provide audit logs but they live in our control plane — we can provide export windows and retention settings.
[04:10] Tom Bennett: Latency and performance for our use cases are important. If we go Private/on-prem, do we lose Redwood optimizations like KV cache?
[04:18] Mateo Ruiz: No, the runtime supports all the same caching and batching on Private deployments; some kernel-level optimizations depend on hardware but feature parity is a priority. We might need to tune batching and kernel selection per deployment.
[04:30] Rachel Lee: Compliance question: for GDPR DSARs, if a customer requests deletion, how quickly can you purge data from hosted?
[04:36] Olivia Park: For Hosted we have deletion API and standard retention windows — deletion requests are processed but there can be short propagation delays. For Dedicated/Private, deletion is under your control so you can do it immediately subject to your infra.
[04:50] Aaron Miles: We have a requirement to keep logs for 7 years for certain custodial accounts. Will retention/archival be configurable?
[04:57] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, archive retention policies can be set on Dedicated/Private; Hosted has configurable retention but extremely long retention might require a Dedicated contract.
[05:06] Sana Iqbal: Network egress — can we restrict egress for EU workloads so that model calls never transit US?
[05:12] Mateo Ruiz: You can pin requests to region-specific endpoints and for Private you run in-region only. Hosted can be region-restricted but subprocessors may be global; we will detail subprocessors per region in the security pack.
[05:24] Tom Bennett: What's the typical timeline for a Private deployment? We have a Q1 2026 pilot goal.
[05:30] Olivia Park: Private on-prem usually 6–10 weeks depending on procurement and infra readiness; Dedicated can be faster if we reserve capacity, often 2–4 weeks. We'll work with your infra team to scope.
[05:42] Rachel Lee: One more — we need SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC integration with our IdP for audit.
[05:49] Mateo Ruiz: Supported. SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning available for Dedicated and Hosted. On Private you can integrate with your IdP directly.
[05:58] Aaron Miles: Any regulatory writeups for financial services you can share, like PCI scoping guidance for AI/LLM vendors?
[06:04] Olivia Park: We'll share a short PCI/controls checklist we use with other banks — it's part of the security pack we'll send.
[06:12] Tom Bennett: Competitors like Anthropic and Bedrock have certain regional commitments; we'd like to see exact subprocessors and the model of isolation.
[06:21] Olivia Park: Yep — we'll include competitor comparison notes as part of follow-up where relevant, but mainly we'll send concrete infra diagrams and our SOPs.
[06:29] Rachel Lee: Ok, next steps?
[06:32] Olivia Park: Recap: We'll send SOC2, GDPR mapping, subprocessors list, PCI checklist, architecture diagram for private deployment, and proposed timeline. Mateo will prepare the tech deep dive. We schedule a follow up for the week of Nov 17.
[06:45] Tom Bennett: Sounds good.
[06:47] Aaron Miles: Thanks everyone.
[06:50] Olivia Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[06:54] --- End of transcript ---

Notes: transcript contains minor ASR errors and occasional speaker mis-attribution. References to PAN and PCI are high-level; customers must consult legal for final scoping.
